channel.description: Recent content in Integrations on tik

item.title: Claude Code skill
item.description:
Install the tik skill into Claude Code and Claude gains working knowledge of tik: it recognises a store, records facts with tik set rather than inventing a status field, reads tik explain before asking a person anything, and authors process definitions whose stages derive from evidence instead of listing activities.

That last part is the reason the skill exists. The failure mode for any model writing a tik process is a task list wearing a process costume — stages named after activities, with nothing following from anything. The skill carries the design law that rules it out, along with the closed guard vocabulary and the authoring loop that checks the result.

item.title: Clojure library
item.description:
tik.api gives a JVM, babashka or native-image program the answers of tik status and tik verify for one ticket without running the CLI. It never writes to the store, signs, runs a probe, touches the network or starts a process.

(require '[tik.api :as api])

(def store (api/open-store "/path/to/.tik")) ; the dir holding tickets/ or tik.db

(api/derive store "f106aa78")
;; => {:ticket #uuid "f106aa78-…" :title "…"
;; :rules {:process :skilled-change :version 2 :hash "sha256-…"}
;; :current [:scoped] :reached [:scoped]
;; :facts {[:kind] {:status :present :value :feat :by "claude"} …}
;; :missing-parents nil
;; :definition {:pinned "sha256-…" :derived-under "sha256-…" :source :archive}
;; :at #inst "…"}

(:ok? (api/verify-ticket store "f106aa78"))

Add tik as a git dependency in deps.edn:

item.title: GitHub Actions
item.description:
tik bridge github --config github.edn # poll once
tik bridge github --config github.edn --webhook # serve workflow_run deliveries

tik bridge github turns failed GitHub Actions runs into tickets under the ci-failure process. One ticket covers one failure streak: the consecutive failed runs of one workflow on one branch, from the first failure after a green run up to the next green run. Further failures attach to the open ticket as ci/run/<id>/<attempt> artifacts, the next green run is recorded as forge.green-run, and a failure after that opens a new ticket. Cancelled, skipped and neutral runs neither extend nor end a streak. GitLab pipelines feed the same process with the same facts, so the metrics below cover both forges.

item.title: GitLab pipelines
item.description:
tik bridge gitlab --config gitlab.edn # poll once

tik bridge gitlab turns failed GitLab pipelines into ci-failure tickets, with the same streak rules, facts and metrics as GitHub Actions . A pipeline has no workflow id; its source (push, schedule, web, …) takes that place, so a failing nightly schedule and green push pipelines on the same branch are separate streaks, titled push pipeline, schedule pipeline and so on. Pipelines with any status other than failed and success (canceled, skipped, manual) neither extend nor end a streak.

item.title: Local service
item.description:
The native binary runs everything a long-running local install needs: tik serve for the board and MCP, tik bridge <kind> sweeps, tik backend for scheduled pipelines and tik notify for hints. It needs no JVM, no babashka and no checkout. Every release checks this with dev/native-smoke.sh, which drives the built binary through each of these against loopback stand-ins for GitHub, GitLab, Redmine, Odoo and an IMAP mailbox.

The environment

Variable Read by Meaning
TIK_ROOT every verb The store. Without it, tik uses the nearest ancestor holding .tik/, tickets/ or tik.db.
TIK_ACTOR every write The actor events are signed as. --actor overrides it.
TIK_KEY every write The ed25519 private key that signs. --key overrides it.
GITHUB_TOKEN bridge github The token when github.edn names neither :token nor :tokens.
GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET bridge github --webhook The HMAC secret when github.edn has no :webhook {:secret …}.
GITLAB_TOKEN bridge gitlab The token when gitlab.edn has no :token.
REDMINE_API_KEY bridge redmine The key when redmine.edn has no :key.
ODOO_PASSWORD bridge odoo The password when odoo.edn has no :password.
CREDENTIALS_DIRECTORY any {:credential …} Set by systemd for LoadCredential=.
XDG_RUNTIME_DIR, XDG_STATE_HOME notify The default socket directory and the cursor.

Any secret in a bridge config can be a spec instead of a literal: {:command "pass show github"} (the first line of the command’s output), {:file "/run/secrets/x"}, {:env "NAME"} or {:credential "NAME"}. The credential form is the one to prefer under systemd: the secret never sits in a file you commit, in the environment or in argv. An unset variable, a missing file, a failing command and an empty or blank value are refused rather than read as an empty secret. A command has one minute to answer, its error output goes to tik’s stderr instead of into the refusal, and a file, credential or output longer than 64 KiB is refused.

item.title: MCP server
item.description:
TIK_ACTOR=bot TIK_KEY=~/.config/tik/bot_ed25519 tik mcp

tik mcp speaks the Model Context Protocol over stdio and exposes one store as a tool surface. The tools an agent is offered are exactly the steps the frontier admits for its role at that moment, so the tool list is the authorization boundary.

One shared server over HTTP

TIK_ACTOR=bot TIK_KEY=~/.config/tik/bot_ed25519 \
 tik serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 7777 --mcp-token-file ~/.local/state/tik/mcp-token

tik serve also speaks MCP on /mcp when given a token file, so every client shares one long-running server instead of starting its own process. It answers one JSON-RPC message per POST with JSON and opens no event stream. A request needs the token as Authorization: Bearer …, and one whose Origin is not the server’s own is refused, which keeps a web page from driving the server through DNS rebinding. The token must be at least 32 characters; openssl rand -hex 32 makes one.

item.title: Odoo
item.description:
tik bridge odoo --config odoo.edn # poll once
tik bridge odoo describe --model project.task --config odoo.edn # read a model's fields

tik bridge odoo mirrors Odoo project tasks into the store as tickets under the odoo-task process. Each ticket carries the task’s title, stage, assignee and project as facts signed by the bridge, its conversation as artifacts, and its URL as odoo.url. The stage follows the mirrored Odoo stage: :closed when the configuration names that stage as closed, :open for every other stage. Moving the task back to an open stage in Odoo brings the ticket back to :open on the next sync.

item.title: Redmine
item.description:
tik bridge redmine --config redmine.edn # poll once

tik bridge redmine mirrors Redmine issues into the store as tickets under the redmine-issue process. Each ticket carries the issue’s status, assignee, priority, tracker, project, subject and due date as facts signed by the bridge, its description and notes as artifacts, and its URL as redmine.url. The stage follows the mirrored status: :open, or :closed when Redmine counts the status as closed. Reopening the issue in Redmine brings the ticket back to :open on the next sync.
